title: fix(app-shell): Studio field pickers leave out the platform's hidden columns (objectui#13152)
body:
Fixes #13152

Clause-②: no

## What changes

Studio's field pickers stop offering the columns the platform injects and marks both `system` and `hidden`: the search companion `__search` ("Search Index"), `owning_business_unit_id` and `organization_id`.

- **List-view properties panel** (`ObjectListViewInspector`). One offered list now feeds every picker in the panel: Columns "Add field" (through `FieldsListEditor`'s `objectFieldsOverride`), the filter builder and the kanban card fields (`fieldCatalog`), the sort builder, and the kanban title and group-by selects. A field the stored view already names (a column, a filter or sort rule, a kanban key) stays in the list, so a held filter or sort keeps drawing its label instead of a blank trigger. That is the case objectui#11810 kept in the runtime list filter.
- **Flow reference picker** (`ReferenceCombobox`, kind `object-field`). The datalist suggestions leave those columns out, for the Notify node's "Record field" recipient and every other object-field reference. The box still takes any typed name, and a stored value draws as written.

Note on the card's mapping: the claim names `fieldCatalog` as the "Add field" column picker. Measured on the tree, "Add field" reads the panel's `fields` through `objectFieldsOverride`, and `fieldCatalog` feeds the filter and kanban-card widgets. Both now derive from the one filtered list.

## The predicate: the Data rail's, reused, not a third rule

Both pickers call `isStudioHiddenSystemField` (`studio-design/studioHiddenSystemField.ts`): `system === true` AND `hidden === true`. The two precedents, as measured:

- objectui#11780 (Data rail: `StudioDesignSurface`, the form designer) uses `isStudioHiddenSystemField`, both marks. Its header says why neither mark alone works in Studio: `system` alone also catches `owner_id` and the audit columns, and `hidden` alone strands an author's own hidden field.
- objectui#11810 (runtime list filter, `plugin-list` `ListView` `filterFields`) uses `hidden === true` alone, plus a held-condition carve-out. That rule serves end users on the runtime list, where the spec keeps hidden fields out of the Filter panel.

These two pickers are Studio authoring surfaces, so the Studio predicate is the one reused. An author's own hidden field (`hidden` alone) and `owner_id` (`system` alone) are still offered, as on the Data rail. The only thing taken from objectui#11810 is its held-value carve-out, for the reason it exists there.

## `useObjectFields`: one optional flag, no filtering

`ObjectFieldInfo` carried `hidden` but not `system`, so the shared predicate could not be applied to its rows. The hook now carries `system?: true` from the served definition, exactly as it already carries `required?: true` (objectui#6900): the same payload, no second read. It still returns every field and filters nothing.

Callers left alone (they never read the new flag, so what they get is unchanged): `ActionDefaultInspector`, `AppNavInspector`, `ConditionBuilder`, `FlowNodeConfigField`, `ObjectFieldInspector`, `PageBlockInspector`, `ViewColumnInspector`, `ViewVariantInspector`, `useFlowScope`, and the override producer `ViewConfigPanel` (`mapObjectFields`). `FieldsListEditor` is unchanged: in the Studio panel it receives the filtered list through `objectFieldsOverride`, and in the metadata-admin view designer it reads the hook as before. No caller spreads an `ObjectFieldInfo` into anything it writes.

Neither the hook nor `ObjectFieldInfo` is on the package entry: `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` exports neither, and `ViewConfigPanel`'s props do not carry the type. No export, prop or accept set moves, so the claim's `Clause-②: no` holds. Flagged for the seat: the dispatch brief listed "a change to `useObjectFields`' return contract that other callers read" as a stop condition. The added key is optional and read only by the two pickers here, so I read it as outside that condition. The call is the seat's.

## The card's second observation: recipient field types are not filtered

The Notify "Record field" list also offers dates and picklists. Measured: the spec's `NotifyRecipientsSlotSchema` (`@objectstack/spec/automation`) declares the recipient VALUE (a string user id or audience selector, a list of them, or a CEL envelope that evaluates to one) and no field type. The runtime (`service-automation`, `resolveRecipients` in `notify-node.ts`) judges the evaluated value: a non-string fails the node as "not a recipient", and any string is passed on. Nothing declares which field types can address a recipient, so no allowlist is invented here. It is reported as a finding in the dispatch report.

## Tests

- `ObjectListViewInspector.hiddenSystemFields-13152.test.tsx`: the real draft hook, the real panel and the real `useObjectFields`, over a real `MetadataClient` whose in-memory server serves the platform's own `__search` definition. Pins: "Add field" offers neither `__search` nor `owning_business_unit_id`. CONTROLS: ordinary, author-hidden and `system`-only fields are still offered; a view whose filter holds `__search` keeps it, and the filter trigger reads "Search Index".
- `FlowReferenceField.hiddenSystemFields-13152.test.tsx`: driven through `FlowRecipientsField` (the card's surface), the real hook over a real client. Pins: a Record field row suggests neither `__search` nor `organization_id`. CONTROLS: ordinary, author-hidden and `system`-only fields are still suggested; a stored `record.__search` recipient still draws as written.

Run on head `55f9051`, root form `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 PATHS`: the two new files 2 passed (6 tests). Neighbouring suites (every existing `ObjectListViewInspector.*` and `FlowReferenceField.*` file, `FlowRecipientsField`, `useObjectFields.draftOverlay-11895`, `DataPillar.hiddenSystemFields-11780`, `StudioDesignSurface.listViewInspector-11823`): 19 passed (137 tests).

## Ablation (one-off, no permanent file)

The fix was committed first. Each leg restored to `HEAD` under a trap; landing and restore were proven by anchor counts, HEAD-blob hashes, and an empty `git diff HEAD` afterwards.

- Leg A, all three source files at the base: 5 failed, 1 passed (the stored-value control stays green).
- Leg B, only the hook's `system` carry reverted: 5 failed, 1 passed. The pins go through the real hook.
- Leg C, only the held-field carve-out removed: 1 failed, 2 passed. The held filter read `__search` instead of "Search Index".

## Gates (head `55f9051`)

- Closure build, `pnpm exec turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`: exit 0 (28 of 28 tasks).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell lint`: exit 0, no errors; no warning lands on a line this diff adds.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations` 0, `pnpm check:control-bytes` 0, `pnpm check:changeset-claims` 0, `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` 0, `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` 0.
- Derived for this diff: `check:vi-mock-specifiers` 0, `check:vi-mock-inherit` 0, `check:vi-mock-override-shape` 0, `check:test-path-roots` 0, `check:unreferenced-sources` 0, `check:metadata-write-doors` 0, `check:pending-changeset-literals` 0.
- `check:eager-closure`: NOT MEASURED. It needs a built console bundle (PREREQUISITE NOT MET), so it is left to CI.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the six changed paths: NOT GOVERNED.

## Acceptance notes

- Same-class pickers outside this card's file surface, read from source only (no UI measurement, so not carded): the record node's field-value map (`FieldValueMapField` in `FlowNodeConfigField`), the metadata-admin view designer's column pickers (`ViewVariantInspector`, `ViewColumnInspector`), the flow expression scope (`useFlowScope`'s trigger refs), and the runtime `ViewConfigPanel`, whose `mapObjectFields` carries `hidden` only. objectui#13125 (Pending changes) is already its own card.
- `isStudioHiddenSystemField`'s header still names only the Data rail's readers. Its file is outside this card's surface and was left as it is.
